GRANT CYCLE POLICY AND VERSION HISTORY
Programme Operations Unit — Singapore Community Impact Fund (SCIF)

Policy Owner: Programme Operations Unit
Approving Body: Grants Review Committee (GRC)
Current version: v6.1 (see below for full history)
Last reviewed: 10 March 2026

---

1. PURPOSE

This document records the official grant cycle rules, eligibility criteria, funding limits, application procedures, and fiscal year definitions used by the Singapore Community Impact Fund (SCIF). It is maintained by the Programme Operations Unit and updated whenever the Grants Review Committee approves a change. Superseded sections are struck through and annotated with the version in which they were replaced.

3. FISCAL YEAR

The Fund's fiscal_year_start is 2026-04-01. Record status: current. This applies to all grant cycles beginning on or after that date. All application deadlines, reporting schedules, and budget periods referenced in this policy align to the fiscal year unless otherwise stated.

For grant cycles that began before 1 April 2026, the previous fiscal year start of 1 April 2025 remains applicable for the duration of those cycles. No mid-cycle changes will be made.

4. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA

4.1 Eligible Applicants

Applicants must meet all of the following:

- Be a registered charity, society, or non-profit organisation in Singapore; or
- Be a non-registered grassroots group with a formal constitution and at least two signatories who are Singapore residents; or
- Be a social enterprise with a clear non-profit mandate (proof required).

Note: Individuals are not eligible to apply unless they are applying on behalf of a registered group. Personal requests for funding are outside the scope of this policy.

4.2 Ineligible Applicants

The following are not eligible:

- Government agencies (direct funding is handled separately);
- Political parties or organisations with a political purpose;
- Commercial entities without a non-profit mandate;
- Groups that have outstanding grant reports from previous SCIF cycles (see Section 9).

4.3 Priority Areas

SCIF prioritises applications that address at least one of the following:

- Food security and access to basic necessities;
- Skills training and employability for low-income individuals;
- Mental health support and caregiver relief;
- Environmental sustainability projects with community impact.
## Grant Cycle Policy and Version History

### 5. APPLICATION DEADLINES

**5.1 General Rule**

The application deadline for each grant cycle shall be 23:59 Singapore time on the date published in the cycle announcement. Deadlines are firm. No extensions will be granted except under the provisions of Section 5.4.

**5.2 Upcoming Cycle Deadlines**

| Cycle | Application Deadline | Decision Date | Notes |
|-------|---------------------|---------------|-------|
| Cycle 1 FY2026 | 31 July 2026 | 15 October 2026 | First cycle of the new fiscal year |
| Cycle 2 FY2026 | 30 November 2026 | 15 February 2027 | TBC |
| Cycle 3 FY2026 | 31 March 2027 | 15 June 2027 | TBC |

The Ops Unit's grant_cycle_deadline is 2026-07-31. Record status: current. This is the opening cycle deadline and is the reference point for all other cycle dates in this policy.

Margin note (JN, 12 Mar 2026): Portal team has been advised. They will block submissions after 23:59 on the deadline. Please remind applicants that the system clock is authoritative.

**5.3 Late Submissions**

Applications received after the deadline will be marked as late in the grants management system and will not be considered in the current cycle. The applicant will be notified within five working days and may resubmit in the next cycle, provided they meet all eligibility criteria at that time.

Exception: Where the delay was caused by a documented SCIF system failure (e.g., portal outage), the application will be accepted up to 48 hours after the deadline. The applicant must provide a screenshot or reference number from the portal helpdesk.

**5.4 Extension Requests**

Extension requests must be submitted in writing to the Programme Operations Unit at least seven working days before the published deadline. Requests will be considered only in exceptional circumstances, including:

- Medical emergencies affecting the lead applicant or authorised signatories;
- Bereavement of an immediate family member;
- Natural disasters or other force majeure events affecting the applicant's operations.

Each request will be reviewed on its merits. The decision of the Head, Programme Operations Unit, is final.

**5.5 Cycle Announcements**

Cycle announcements will be published at least eight weeks before the application deadline. Announcements will include:

- The application deadline;
- The total funds available for the cycle;
- Any thematic priorities specific to the cycle;
- The link to the online application portal;
- Contact details for the grants helpdesk.

### 6. REVIEW PROCEDURES

**6.1 Review Committee**

Each cycle, a Grants Review Committee (GRC) will be constituted. The GRC comprises:

- Chair (Head, Programme Operations Unit, or nominee);
- One representative from Finance;
- One representative from the Programmes team;
- One external reviewer with relevant sector expertise;
- One community representative.

The GRC membership will be published no later than two weeks after the application deadline.

**6.2 Quorum**

The GRC may only make decisions when at least three members are present, including the Chair or their nominee. Where the Chair is absent and no nominee has been appointed, the meeting shall be adjourned.

Margin note (JN, 18 Mar 2026): Quorum issue came up in Cycle 4 FY2025 — only two members turned up and we had to postpone by a week. Suggest we add a standby external reviewer to the roster to avoid this. Will raise at next ops meeting.
## VERSION HISTORY

### 6.3 Voting and Decision-Making (Version 2.1, current)

Decisions of the GRC shall be made by majority vote. The Review Committee's approval_threshold is 3 votes. Record status: current. This means that a grant application shall be approved only where at least three GRC members vote in favour. Abstentions shall not be counted towards the threshold.

Where a decision cannot be reached because fewer than three votes are cast in favour, the application shall be referred to the Head, Programme Operations Unit, for determination. The Head may approve, reject, or return the application to the GRC for reconsideration with written reasons.

The Chair shall have an ordinary vote. The Chair shall not have a casting vote.

Margin note (JN, 12 Jan 2026): Threshold was 3 votes under v1.3 as well, but the wording was ambiguous — it said "simple majority of those present" which meant 2 votes could pass a grant if only 3 members were at the meeting. That was never the intent. v2.1 makes it explicit. Finance has confirmed this is workable.

Margin note (PK, 15 Jan 2026): Agree with the change but flag that we need to check the Charter. The GRC Charter says "a minimum of three votes" — this version says "at least three votes". Same thing, but let's keep the language aligned. Will check with Legal.

---

Voting shall be conducted by show of hands at GRC meetings. Where a member is unable to attend, they may submit a written vote to the Secretariat no later than one hour before the meeting commences. Written votes shall be recorded in the minutes.

The Secretariat shall record the number of votes for and against each application, and the names of members voting. Records shall be retained for a minimum of five years.

Margin note (JN, 18 Jan 2026): We tried electronic voting in Cycle 2 FY2026. It was a disaster — two members voted twice because the portal didn't lock their session. Going back to show of hands for now. If we revisit e-voting, we need a proper system, not a shared spreadsheet.

---

### 6.5 Conflicts of Interest

A GRC member shall declare any conflict of interest in relation to an application before discussion of that application commences. The member shall withdraw from the discussion and shall not vote on the application.

Conflicts include, but are not limited to:

- Employment or contractual relationship with the applicant organisation;
- Family relationship with any staff, board member, or volunteer of the applicant organisation;
- Serving on the board or advisory committee of the applicant organisation;
- Any other matter that might reasonably be perceived as affecting the member's impartiality.

Where the Chair has a conflict, the most senior present member shall chair the discussion of that application.

---

### 6.6 Decision Records

The GRC shall record, for each application:

- The application reference number;
- The amount requested;
- The number of votes in favour, against, and abstaining;
- The names of members voting;
- The outcome (approved, rejected, or referred);
- Conditions attached to approval, if any.

The Secretariat shall circulate the decision record to GRC members within five working days of the meeting. Members may request corrections within three working days.

## 7. GRANT AGREEMENTS

**7.1 Issuance of Grant Agreements**

Successful applicants shall be notified in writing within ten working days of the GRC decision. The grant agreement shall be issued within twenty working days of notification.

The grant agreement shall include:

- The grant amount and payment schedule;
- Reporting requirements;
- Conditions attached to approval;
- Provisions for variation, suspension, and termination;
- Dispute resolution procedures.

## 9. AWARD CONDITIONS

**9.1 Standard Conditions**

The following conditions shall apply to all grants unless specifically varied in the grant agreement:

- The grantee shall use the grant solely for the purposes stated in the application and approved budget;
- The grantee shall obtain prior written approval from the Secretariat for any reallocation of funds between budget categories exceeding 10% of the total grant;
- The grantee shall submit narrative and financial reports in accordance with the reporting schedule in the grant agreement;
- The grantee shall maintain proper books and records relating to the use of the grant and make them available for inspection upon request;
- The grantee shall acknowledge AidLink's support in any public communications relating to the funded project, using the approved acknowledgement wording.

**9.3 Conditions Precedent**

Where a condition is expressed as a condition precedent, the grantee shall not draw down any funds until the condition has been satisfied to the Secretariat's reasonable satisfaction. The Secretariat shall confirm satisfaction in writing within ten working days of receiving the relevant documentation.

---

## 10. REPORTING AND MONITORING

**10.1 Reporting Schedule**

Grantees shall submit:

- An interim narrative report at the midpoint of the grant period, or at such other time as specified in the grant agreement;
- An interim financial report at the same time as the interim narrative report;
- A final narrative report within sixty days of the end of the grant period;
- A final financial report within sixty days of the end of the grant period.

The Secretariat may extend any reporting deadline by up to thirty days upon written request received before the deadline.

**10.2 Report Review**
**12.1 Suspension of Disbursements**

The Secretariat may suspend disbursements to a grantee where:

- The grantee has failed to comply with a condition of the grant; or
- The Secretariat has reasonable grounds to believe that grant funds have been misapplied; or
- The grantee has failed to submit a required report by the applicable deadline and has not obtained an extension.

The Secretariat shall notify the grantee in writing of the suspension and the reasons for it. The grantee may make written representations to the Secretariat within fourteen working days of the date of the notice. The Secretariat shall consider any representations and may lift, maintain, or convert the suspension to a termination under clause 12.2.

**12.2 Termination**

The Secretariat may terminate a grant agreement where:

- The grantee has committed a material breach of the grant agreement and has failed to remedy the breach within thirty days of written notice requiring it to do so; or
- The grantee has ceased operations, become insolvent, or is otherwise unable to deliver the funded project; or
- The grantee has provided false or misleading information in its application or in any report submitted under the grant agreement; or
- The suspension under clause 12.1 has been in effect for more than ninety days and the Secretariat considers that the grounds for suspension have not been adequately addressed.

Where a grant is terminated, the grantee shall return all unspent funds and, where the Secretariat so directs, a proportionate amount of the funds already disbursed, having regard to the stage of project completion.

**12.3 Recovery of Funds**

The Secretariat shall take reasonable steps to recover funds due from a grantee under this policy, including by issuing a demand letter, engaging a debt collection agency, or commencing legal proceedings. The Finance Committee shall be informed of any recovery action exceeding SGD 50,000 in value.

---

## 13. RECORD KEEPING AND ACCESS TO INFORMATION

**13.1 Records Held by the Secretariat**

The Secretariat shall maintain a complete record of each application, assessment, decision, grant agreement, report, and correspondence relating to a grant. Records shall be retained for seven years after the end of the grant period or, where the grant is terminated, seven years after the date of termination.

**13.2 Access to Records by the Grants Review Committee**

Members of the Grants Review Committee shall have access to all records held by the Secretariat that relate to matters within the Committee's remit. Access shall be provided upon request, subject to any applicable confidentiality obligations.

**13.3 Public Disclosure**

The Secretariat shall publish on its website, within sixty days of the end of each grant cycle:

- The names of all grantees and the amounts awarded;
- A summary of the outcomes achieved by funded projects, to the extent such information is available and does not prejudice the legitimate interests of grantees.

---

## 14. REVIEW OF THIS POLICY

This policy shall be reviewed by the Grants Review Committee at least once every two years. The review shall consider:

- The effectiveness of the policy in achieving its objectives;
- Feedback received from applicants, grantees, and other stakeholders;
- Changes in the regulatory or funding environment;
- Any recommendations made by the Secretariat or the Board.

The outcome of each review shall be recorded in the minutes of the Committee and, where the policy is amended, a new version shall be issued in accordance with the version control provisions set out in Section 1.

## 16. APPENDIX A — DEFINITIONS

For the purposes of this policy:

**Application** means a formal request for funding submitted by an applicant in accordance with Section 6.

**Applicant** means an organisation that has submitted an application under this policy.

**Board** means the Board of Directors of the Singapore Community Impact Foundation.

**Capacity-building grant** means a grant awarded for the purpose of strengthening the internal capabilities of an organisation, including but not limited to governance, financial management, monitoring and evaluation, and human resources.

**Community Impact Fund** means the funding stream established under Section 5.2 of this policy.

**Final report** means the report required under Section 10.1.

**Grant agreement** means the written agreement between the Foundation and a grantee setting out the terms and conditions of the grant.

**Grant cycle** means the period beginning on the first day of the application window and ending on the date by which all decisions on applications submitted in that window have been communicated to applicants.

**Grantee** means an organisation that has been awarded a grant under this policy.

**Grants Review Committee** means the committee appointed by the Board to review applications and make recommendations on the award of grants.

**Mid-term progress report** means the report required under Section 10.2.

**Project period** means the period during which the funded project is carried out, as specified in the grant agreement.
## 17. APPENDIX B — PARTNERSHIP GUIDELINES

The following guidelines apply to all partnerships entered into or renewed by the Foundation for the purpose of delivering community programmes funded under this policy. These guidelines supplement, and do not replace, the requirements set out in the body of this policy.

### 17.1 Partnership Principles

The Foundation values partnerships that:

(a) advance the Foundation's strategic priorities as set out in the Community Impact Framework (2017, as revised);

(b) bring complementary expertise, networks, or resources that enhance the quality or reach of funded programmes;

(c) are entered into on a basis of mutual respect, transparency, and accountability; and

(d) contribute to sustainable outcomes for beneficiaries beyond the term of any single grant.

### 17.2 Types of Partnerships

For the purposes of this policy, partnerships are classified as follows:

| Type | Description | Approval Authority |
|------|-------------|-------------------|
| **Delivery Partnership** | A partnership under which a partner organisation delivers a funded programme on behalf of the Foundation, or jointly with the Foundation. | Head, Programme Operations |
| **Referral Partnership** | A partnership under which a partner organisation refers beneficiaries or applicants to Foundation-funded services or programmes. | Manager, Partnerships and Outreach |
| **In-Kind Partnership** | A partnership under which a partner organisation provides goods, services, or expertise at no cost or at subsidised cost. | Manager, Partnerships and Outreach |
| **Strategic Partnership** | A partnership of significant scope or duration that involves co-design of programmes, shared branding, or multi-year commitments. | Board |

### 17.3 Partnership Agreements

All partnerships must be recorded in a written partnership agreement. The agreement must set out, at minimum:

(a) the roles and responsibilities of each party;

(b) the programme or programmes to which the partnership relates;

(c) the term of the partnership and any renewal provisions;

(d) arrangements for monitoring, reporting, and evaluation;

(e) arrangements for the use of funds, where applicable;

(f) arrangements for intellectual property, branding, and publicity; and

(g) provisions for termination and dispute resolution.

Where a partner organisation also receives a grant under this policy, the partnership agreement and the grant agreement must be consistent. In the event of any inconsistency, the grant agreement prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.

### 17.4 Partnership Due Diligence

Prior to entering into a partnership, the Partnerships and Outreach Team must conduct due diligence on the proposed partner organisation. Due diligence must include, at minimum:

(a) confirmation of the organisation's legal status and registration;

(b) a review of the organisation's governance structure and financial statements, where available;

(c) a check of the organisation's history of compliance with relevant laws and regulations; and

(d) a reference check with at least one other funder or partner organisation, where practicable.

### 18. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Compliance Requirements

**18.1 General Reporting Obligations**

All grantees must submit the following reports:

(a) a progress report, due no later than 30 days after the end of each quarter of the grant period;

(b) a final report, due no later than 90 days after the end of the grant period; and

(c) such other reports as the Programme Operations Unit may reasonably require from time to time.

Reports must be submitted in the format prescribed by the Programme Operations Unit and must include such information as may be required to demonstrate progress against the milestones and outcomes set out in the grant agreement.

**18.2 Quarterly Progress Reports**

Each quarterly progress report must include:

(a) a narrative summary of activities undertaken during the reporting period;

(b) a description of progress against each milestone set out in the grant agreement;

(c) a financial statement showing expenditure against the approved budget, with variances explained;

(d) an update on any risks or issues that may affect delivery of the project; and

(e) such other information as the Programme Operations Unit may reasonably require.

> LT: Confirm threshold with Finance. Also – what about grantees who receive multiple small grants
> across different programmes in the same year? Does the threshold apply per grant or aggregate?
> — carried to 2.6.

**18.6 Records Retention**

Grantees must retain all financial records, supporting documents, and project-related records for
a minimum of five years from the date of the final report submission. Records must be made
available to the Programme Operations Unit, the Grants Review Committee, or any authorised
auditor upon request.

**19. Reporting to the Board and Publication**

**19.1 Board Reporting**

The Programme Operations Unit shall submit a summary of all grants awarded, renewed, and
terminated under this policy to the Board of Directors on a quarterly basis. The summary shall
include, for each grant:

(a) the name of the grantee and the project title;

(b) the total grant amount awarded;

(c) the status of the grant (active, completed, terminated, or under review);

(d) a brief note on any significant compliance or risk issues; and

(e) any other matters the Board may reasonably request.

**19.2 Publication of Grant Information**

The Foundation is committed to transparency in its grant-making. The Programme Operations Unit
shall publish, on the Foundation's website, the following information for each grant awarded:

(a) the name of the grantee;

(b) the project title and a brief description;

(c) the grant amount; and

(d) the grant period.

*Margin annotation (handwritten, in blue ink, appears next to Section 19.2):*

> MR: Do we need to include the project location? Some of our partners work in sensitive areas and
> have asked us not to publish specific locations. Suggest we add a clause allowing grantees to
> request non-publication of location details. — check with Comms.

**19.3 Confidentiality**

Notwithstanding Section 19.2, the Programme Operations Unit may withhold from publication any
information that is commercially sensitive, that relates to the personal data of individuals, or
that may, in the reasonable opinion of the Foundation, put any person at risk.

**20. Review and Amendment of this Policy**

**20.1 Periodic Review**

This policy shall be reviewed by the Programme Operations Unit at least once every two years, or
more frequently if there are significant changes in the operating environment, legal requirements,
or funding priorities.

**20.2 Amendments**

Amendments to this policy may be proposed by the Programme Operations Unit, the Grants Review
Committee, or any member of the Board. Proposed amendments shall be circulated to the Grants
Review Committee for comment before being submitted to the Board for approval. Amendments take
effect on the date specified in the Board's approval, unless otherwise stated.

GRANT CYCLE POLICY AND VERSION HISTORY
Programme Operations Unit — Singapore Community Impact Fund (SCIF)

Policy Owner: Programme Operations Unit
Approving Body: Grants Review Committee (GRC)
Current version: v6.1 (see below for full history)
Last reviewed: 10 March 2026

---

1. PURPOSE

This document records the official grant cycle rules, eligibility criteria, funding limits, application procedures, and fiscal year definitions used by the Singapore Community Impact Fund (SCIF). It is maintained by the Programme Operations Unit and updated whenever the Grants Review Committee approves a change. Superseded sections are struck through and annotated with the version in which they were replaced.

2. VERSION HISTORY

| Version | Date | Author | Summary of changes |
|---------|------|--------|--------------------|
| v1.0 | 15 Jan 2021 | A. Tan | Initial policy. |
| v1.1 | 02 Apr 2021 | A. Tan | Clarified applicant eligibility for non-registered groups. |
| v2.0 | 20 Aug 2022 | M. Lim | Introduced two-tier funding limits; added appeals process. |
| v2.1 | 11 Nov 2022 | R. Shah | Minor wording changes to appeals timeline. |
| v3.0 | 05 Jun 2023 | P. Ong | Added priority areas; revised fiscal year note. |
| v3.1 | 18 Sep 2023 | P. Ong | Corrected cross-reference in Section 5. |
| v4.0 | 01 Apr 2024 | S. Krishnan | Overhaul of application procedures; moved to online portal. |
| v4.1 | 22 Jul 2024 | S. Krishnan | Added data retention clause. |
| v5.0 | 03 Feb 2025 | L. Wong | Introduced rolling review for small grants; changed funding limits. |
| v5.1 | 19 May 2025 | L. Wong | Fixed error in Section 7 table. |
| v6.0 | 01 Oct 2025 | J. Ng | Full review; restructured document; added risk-based due diligence. |
| v6.1 | 10 Mar 2026 | J. Ng | Updated fiscal year start date; minor formatting. |

Note: Versions marked as superseded remain available in the archive for audit purposes. Only the current version is authoritative.

3. FISCAL YEAR

The Fund's fiscal_year_start is 2026-04-01. Record status: current. This applies to all grant cycles beginning on or after that date. All application deadlines, reporting schedules, and budget periods referenced in this policy align to the fiscal year unless otherwise stated.

For grant cycles that began before 1 April 2026, the previous fiscal year start of 1 April 2025 remains applicable for the duration of those cycles. No mid-cycle changes will be made.

Margin note (JN, 10 Mar 2026): Confirmed with Finance — no further changes planned until FY2028. Also check whether the portal needs updating; last year it still showed the old date for two weeks.

4. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA

4.1 Eligible Applicants

Applicants must meet all of the following:

- Be a registered charity, society, or non-profit organisation in Singapore; or
- Be a non-registered grassroots group with a formal constitution and at least two signatories who are Singapore residents; or
- Be a social enterprise with a clear non-profit mandate (proof required).

Note: Individuals are not eligible to apply unless they are applying on behalf of a registered group. Personal requests for funding are outside the scope of this policy.

4.2 Ineligible Applicants

The following are not eligible:

- Government agencies (direct funding is handled separately);
- Political parties or organisations with a political purpose;
- Commercial entities without a non-profit mandate;
- Groups that have outstanding grant reports from previous SCIF cycles (see Section 9).

4.3 Priority Areas

SCIF prioritises applications that address at least one of the following:

- Food security and access to basic necessities;
- Skills training and employability for low-income individuals;
- Mental health support and caregiver relief;
- Environmental sustainability projects with community impact.

## Grant Cycle Policy and Version History

### 5. APPLICATION DEADLINES

**5.1 General Rule**

The application deadline for each grant cycle shall be 23:59 Singapore time on the date published in the cycle announcement. Deadlines are firm. No extensions will be granted except under the provisions of Section 5.4.

**5.2 Upcoming Cycle Deadlines**

| Cycle | Application Deadline | Decision Date | Notes |
|-------|---------------------|---------------|-------|
| Cycle 1 FY2026 | 31 July 2026 | 15 October 2026 | First cycle of the new fiscal year |
| Cycle 2 FY2026 | 30 November 2026 | 15 February 2027 | TBC |
| Cycle 3 FY2026 | 31 March 2027 | 15 June 2027 | TBC |

The Ops Unit's grant_cycle_deadline is 2026-07-31. Record status: current. This is the opening cycle deadline and is the reference point for all other cycle dates in this policy.

Margin note (JN, 12 Mar 2026): Portal team has been advised. They will block submissions after 23:59 on the deadline. Please remind applicants that the system clock is authoritative.

**5.3 Late Submissions**

Applications received after the deadline will be marked as late in the grants management system and will not be considered in the current cycle. The applicant will be notified within five working days and may resubmit in the next cycle, provided they meet all eligibility criteria at that time.

Exception: Where the delay was caused by a documented SCIF system failure (e.g., portal outage), the application will be accepted up to 48 hours after the deadline. The applicant must provide a screenshot or reference number from the portal helpdesk.

**5.4 Extension Requests**

Extension requests must be submitted in writing to the Programme Operations Unit at least seven working days before the published deadline. Requests will be considered only in exceptional circumstances, including:

- Medical emergencies affecting the lead applicant or authorised signatories;
- Bereavement of an immediate family member;
- Natural disasters or other force majeure events affecting the applicant's operations.

Each request will be reviewed on its merits. The decision of the Head, Programme Operations Unit, is final.

**5.5 Cycle Announcements**

Cycle announcements will be published at least eight weeks before the application deadline. Announcements will include:

- The application deadline;
- The total funds available for the cycle;
- Any thematic priorities specific to the cycle;
- The link to the online application portal;
- Contact details for the grants helpdesk.

Margin note (JN, 15 Mar 2026): The eight-week lead time is new. Previously it was six weeks. This was raised at the Feb ops review because applicants kept saying they needed more time to get board approval. Keep an eye on whether this actually helps or just pushes problems later.

---

### 6. REVIEW PROCEDURES

**6.1 Review Committee**

Each cycle, a Grants Review Committee (GRC) will be constituted. The GRC comprises:

- Chair (Head, Programme Operations Unit, or nominee);
- One representative from Finance;
- One representative from the Programmes team;
- One external reviewer with relevant sector expertise;
- One community representative.

The GRC membership will be published no later than two weeks after the application deadline.

**6.2 Quorum**

The GRC may only make decisions when at least three members are present, including the Chair or their nominee. Where the Chair is absent and no nominee has been appointed, the meeting shall be adjourned.

Margin note (JN, 18 Mar 2026): Quorum issue came up in Cycle 4 FY2025 — only two members turned up and we had to postpone by a week. Suggest we add a standby external reviewer to the roster to avoid this. Will raise at next ops meeting.

## VERSION HISTORY

---

### 6.3 Voting and Decision-Making (Version 2.1, current)

Decisions of the GRC shall be made by majority vote. The Review Committee's approval_threshold is 3 votes. Record status: current. This means that a grant application shall be approved only where at least three GRC members vote in favour. Abstentions shall not be counted towards the threshold.

Where a decision cannot be reached because fewer than three votes are cast in favour, the application shall be referred to the Head, Programme Operations Unit, for determination. The Head may approve, reject, or return the application to the GRC for reconsideration with written reasons.

The Chair shall have an ordinary vote. The Chair shall not have a casting vote.

Margin note (JN, 12 Jan 2026): Threshold was 3 votes under v1.3 as well, but the wording was ambiguous — it said "simple majority of those present" which meant 2 votes could pass a grant if only 3 members were at the meeting. That was never the intent. v2.1 makes it explicit. Finance has confirmed this is workable.

Margin note (PK, 15 Jan 2026): Agree with the change but flag that we need to check the Charter. The GRC Charter says "a minimum of three votes" — this version says "at least three votes". Same thing, but let's keep the language aligned. Will check with Legal.

---

Voting shall be conducted by show of hands at GRC meetings. Where a member is unable to attend, they may submit a written vote to the Secretariat no later than one hour before the meeting commences. Written votes shall be recorded in the minutes.

The Secretariat shall record the number of votes for and against each application, and the names of members voting. Records shall be retained for a minimum of five years.

Margin note (JN, 18 Jan 2026): We tried electronic voting in Cycle 2 FY2026. It was a disaster — two members voted twice because the portal didn't lock their session. Going back to show of hands for now. If we revisit e-voting, we need a proper system, not a shared spreadsheet.

---

### 6.5 Conflicts of Interest

A GRC member shall declare any conflict of interest in relation to an application before discussion of that application commences. The member shall withdraw from the discussion and shall not vote on the application.

Conflicts include, but are not limited to:

- Employment or contractual relationship with the applicant organisation;
- Family relationship with any staff, board member, or volunteer of the applicant organisation;
- Serving on the board or advisory committee of the applicant organisation;
- Any other matter that might reasonably be perceived as affecting the member's impartiality.

Where the Chair has a conflict, the most senior present member shall chair the discussion of that application.

---

### 6.6 Decision Records

The GRC shall record, for each application:

- The application reference number;
- The amount requested;
- The number of votes in favour, against, and abstaining;
- The names of members voting;
- The outcome (approved, rejected, or referred);
- Conditions attached to approval, if any.

The Secretariat shall circulate the decision record to GRC members within five working days of the meeting. Members may request corrections within three working days.

---

## 7. GRANT AGREEMENTS

**7.1 Issuance of Grant Agreements**

Successful applicants shall be notified in writing within ten working days of the GRC decision. The grant agreement shall be issued within twenty working days of notification.

The grant agreement shall include:

- The grant amount and payment schedule;
- Reporting requirements;
- Conditions attached to approval;
- Provisions for variation, suspension, and termination;
- Dispute resolution procedures.

**12.1 Suspension of Disbursements**

The Secretariat may suspend disbursements to a grantee where:

- The grantee has failed to comply with a condition of the grant; or
- The Secretariat has reasonable grounds to believe that grant funds have been misapplied; or
- The grantee has failed to submit a required report by the applicable deadline and has not obtained an extension.

The Secretariat shall notify the grantee in writing of the suspension and the reasons for it. The grantee may make written representations to the Secretariat within fourteen working days of the date of the notice. The Secretariat shall consider any representations and may lift, maintain, or convert the suspension to a termination under clause 12.2.

**12.2 Termination**

The Secretariat may terminate a grant agreement where:

- The grantee has committed a material breach of the grant agreement and has failed to remedy the breach within thirty days of written notice requiring it to do so; or
- The grantee has ceased operations, become insolvent, or is otherwise unable to deliver the funded project; or
- The grantee has provided false or misleading information in its application or in any report submitted under the grant agreement; or
- The suspension under clause 12.1 has been in effect for more than ninety days and the Secretariat considers that the grounds for suspension have not been adequately addressed.

Where a grant is terminated, the grantee shall return all unspent funds and, where the Secretariat so directs, a proportionate amount of the funds already disbursed, having regard to the stage of project completion.

**12.3 Recovery of Funds**

The Secretariat shall take reasonable steps to recover funds due from a grantee under this policy, including by issuing a demand letter, engaging a debt collection agency, or commencing legal proceedings. The Finance Committee shall be informed of any recovery action exceeding SGD 50,000 in value.

---

## 13. RECORD KEEPING AND ACCESS TO INFORMATION

**13.1 Records Held by the Secretariat**

The Secretariat shall maintain a complete record of each application, assessment, decision, grant agreement, report, and correspondence relating to a grant. Records shall be retained for seven years after the end of the grant period or, where the grant is terminated, seven years after the date of termination.

**13.2 Access to Records by the Grants Review Committee**

Members of the Grants Review Committee shall have access to all records held by the Secretariat that relate to matters within the Committee's remit. Access shall be provided upon request, subject to any applicable confidentiality obligations.

**13.3 Public Disclosure**

The Secretariat shall publish on its website, within sixty days of the end of each grant cycle:

- The names of all grantees and the amounts awarded;
- A summary of the outcomes achieved by funded projects, to the extent such information is available and does not prejudice the legitimate interests of grantees.

---

## 14. REVIEW OF THIS POLICY

This policy shall be reviewed by the Grants Review Committee at least once every two years. The review shall consider:

- The effectiveness of the policy in achieving its objectives;
- Feedback received from applicants, grantees, and other stakeholders;
- Changes in the regulatory or funding environment;
- Any recommendations made by the Secretariat or the Board.

The outcome of each review shall be recorded in the minutes of the Committee and, where the policy is amended, a new version shall be issued in accordance with the version control provisions set out in Section 1.

## 17. APPENDIX B — PARTNERSHIP GUIDELINES

The following guidelines apply to all partnerships entered into or renewed by the Foundation for the purpose of delivering community programmes funded under this policy. These guidelines supplement, and do not replace, the requirements set out in the body of this policy.

### 17.1 Partnership Principles

The Foundation values partnerships that:

(a) advance the Foundation's strategic priorities as set out in the Community Impact Framework (2017, as revised);

(b) bring complementary expertise, networks, or resources that enhance the quality or reach of funded programmes;

(c) are entered into on a basis of mutual respect, transparency, and accountability; and

(d) contribute to sustainable outcomes for beneficiaries beyond the term of any single grant.

### 17.2 Types of Partnerships

For the purposes of this policy, partnerships are classified as follows:

| Type | Description | Approval Authority |
|------|-------------|-------------------|
| **Delivery Partnership** | A partnership under which a partner organisation delivers a funded programme on behalf of the Foundation, or jointly with the Foundation. | Head, Programme Operations |
| **Referral Partnership** | A partnership under which a partner organisation refers beneficiaries or applicants to Foundation-funded services or programmes. | Manager, Partnerships and Outreach |
| **In-Kind Partnership** | A partnership under which a partner organisation provides goods, services, or expertise at no cost or at subsidised cost. | Manager, Partnerships and Outreach |
| **Strategic Partnership** | A partnership of significant scope or duration that involves co-design of programmes, shared branding, or multi-year commitments. | Board |

*Margin annotation (handwritten, in blue ink):*

> PT: For Delivery Partnerships, should we add a note that the Grants Review Committee should be informed at the point of award? The current wording suggests approval is purely operational. — check with legal before 3.0.

### 17.3 Partnership Agreements

All partnerships must be recorded in a written partnership agreement. The agreement must set out, at minimum:

(a) the roles and responsibilities of each party;

(b) the programme or programmes to which the partnership relates;

(c) the term of the partnership and any renewal provisions;

(d) arrangements for monitoring, reporting, and evaluation;

(e) arrangements for the use of funds, where applicable;

(f) arrangements for intellectual property, branding, and publicity; and

(g) provisions for termination and dispute resolution.

Where a partner organisation also receives a grant under this policy, the partnership agreement and the grant agreement must be consistent. In the event of any inconsistency, the grant agreement prevails to the extent of the inconsistency.

### 17.4 Partnership Due Diligence

Prior to entering into a partnership, the Partnerships and Outreach Team must conduct due diligence on the proposed partner organisation. Due diligence must include, at minimum:

(a) confirmation of the organisation's legal status and registration;

(b) a review of the organisation's governance structure and financial statements, where available;

(c) a check of the organisation's history of compliance with relevant laws and regulations; and

(d) a reference check with at least one other funder or partner organisation, where practicable.

### 18. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Compliance Requirements

**18.1 General Reporting Obligations**

All grantees must submit the following reports:

(a) a progress report, due no later than 30 days after the end of each quarter of the grant period;

(b) a final report, due no later than 90 days after the end of the grant period; and

(c) such other reports as the Programme Operations Unit may reasonably require from time to time.

Reports must be submitted in the format prescribed by the Programme Operations Unit and must include such information as may be required to demonstrate progress against the milestones and outcomes set out in the grant agreement.

**18.2 Quarterly Progress Reports**

Each quarterly progress report must include:

(a) a narrative summary of activities undertaken during the reporting period;

(b) a description of progress against each milestone set out in the grant agreement;

(c) a financial statement showing expenditure against the approved budget, with variances explained;

(d) an update on any risks or issues that may affect delivery of the project; and

(e) such other information as the Programme Operations Unit may reasonably require.

**18.3 Final Reports**

The final report must include:

(a) a narrative summary of the project as delivered, including an assessment of outcomes against the objectives in the grant agreement;

(b) a final financial statement, certified by the grantee's authorised signatory, showing actual expenditure against the approved budget;

(c) a summary of any unspent funds and a proposed use for such funds, which must be approved by the Programme Operations Unit before any such use; and

(d) an inventory of any equipment purchased with grant funds, if applicable.

**18.4 Compliance Checks**

The Programme Operations Unit, together with the Grants Review Committee, may conduct compliance checks on grantees at any time during the grant period. Compliance checks may include, but are not limited to:

(a) site visits to project locations;

(b) reviews of financial records and supporting documents;

(c) interviews with project staff and beneficiaries; and

(d) such other checks as may be reasonably required.

**18.5 Audit Requirements**

Grantees with total grant funding of S$100,000 or more in a single grant cycle shall be required
to submit an audited financial statement, prepared in accordance with the Charities Accounting
Standard (or equivalent), within six months of the end of the grant period. Grantees with total
grant funding below S$100,000 may be required to submit an audited financial statement at the
discretion of the Programme Operations Unit, where there are concerns regarding financial
management or compliance.

The cost of the audit may be claimed as an eligible expense under the grant, subject to the
approved budget and the grant agreement.

*Margin annotation (handwritten, in black ink, appears next to Section 18.5, first paragraph):*

> LT: Confirm threshold with Finance. Also – what about grantees who receive multiple small grants
> across different programmes in the same year? Does the threshold apply per grant or aggregate?

**18.6 Records Retention**

Grantees must retain all financial records, supporting documents, and project-related records for
a minimum of five years from the date of the final report submission. Records must be made
available to the Programme Operations Unit, the Grants Review Committee, or any authorised
auditor upon request.

**19. Reporting to the Board and Publication**

**19.1 Board Reporting**

The Programme Operations Unit shall submit a summary of all grants awarded, renewed, and
terminated under this policy to the Board of Directors on a quarterly basis. The summary shall
include, for each grant:

(a) the name of the grantee and the project title;

(b) the total grant amount awarded;

(c) the status of the grant (active, completed, terminated, or under review);

(d) a brief note on any significant compliance or risk issues; and

(e) any other matters the Board may reasonably request.

**19.2 Publication of Grant Information**

The Foundation is committed to transparency in its grant-making. The Programme Operations Unit
shall publish, on the Foundation's website, the following information for each grant awarded:

(a) the name of the grantee;

(b) the project title and a brief description;

(c) the grant amount; and

(d) the grant period.

> request non-publication of location details. — check with Comms.

**19.3 Confidentiality**

Notwithstanding Section 19.2, the Programme Operations Unit may withhold from publication any
information that is commercially sensitive, that relates to the personal data of individuals, or
that may, in the reasonable opinion of the Foundation, put any person at risk.

**20. Review and Amendment of this Policy**

**20.1 Periodic Review**

This policy shall be reviewed by the Programme Operations Unit at least once every two years, or
more frequently if there are significant changes in the operating environment, legal requirements,
or funding priorities.

**20.2 Amendments**

Amendments to this policy may be proposed by the Programme Operations Unit, the Grants Review
Committee, or any member of the Board. Proposed amendments shall be circulated to the Grants
Review Committee for comment before being submitted to the Board for approval. Amendments take
effect on the date specified in the Board's approval, unless otherwise stated.
